messages:
Maria: Heads-up — customer Paul reported a sharp increase in 5xx/timeouts this morning for hosted inference. They say requests either time out at 30s or return 502/504. Happening across their tenant us-east-1. Link to request traces: https://console.redwood.co/requests/abcd
Paul (Customer): seeing p95 jump from ~200ms to 6-10s, p99 spikes to 18-22s, occasional 504s. Happened right after a traffic burst around 08:12 UTC. Using model rdx-3b-quant with continuous batching.
Maria: @jonathan can you triage? customer is on a paid plan and flagged it P1.
Jonathan - SRE: On it. Quick summary from logs: ingress shows sustained queue_depth ~= 120 per host, batcher backlog growing, KV cache hit rate dropped ~40%. Also saw a surge of single-token short requests which prevents efficient batching.
Lee - Infra: queue_depth 120 sounds high. What is the configured queue_depth_limit on their host pools?
Anya - EngRuntime: For that pool profile, typical queue limit is 64. If we're seeing 120 it means one of the fallback routes spilled traffic to a less restricted pool or the config didn't apply.
Jonathan - SRE: Pulling host labels... looks like the requests routed to pool "shared-lowlatency-1" which still had legacy queue_limit 128 from a prior rollout. (reacted :eyes:)
DeployBot: Deployment 2026-03-15T07:50:12 rolled: runtime-config v2.14 -> v2.15 to shared-lowlatency-1 (change: temporary queue_limit override=128).
Maria: That explains it — earlier change temporarily increased queue_limit to avoid early rejects during a canary; we may have left it high. Customer saw traffic burst and continuous batching window allowed big prefixes to queue.
Paul (Customer): Any repro steps I can run to show you the pattern? I can replay a minute of their traffic.
Jonathan - SRE: Yes please. Replay 08:12-08:14 traces to the staging replay tool. Repro is helpful. Meanwhile I'll look at batcher metrics.
Anya - EngRuntime: Key symptoms for continuous batching backlog: long-running small requests + high queue_limit + KV cache churn. The runtime tries to fill batches which increases latency for short queries — yields tail-latency.
Lee - Infra: Current mitigation options: 1) reduce queue_limit back to 64 on that pool; 2) enable per-tenant early-reject threshold for that tenant to force immediate 429s instead of backlog; 3) temporarily route heavy tenant to dedicated pool. Which do we want?
Maria: Customer prefers success over errors, but 20s p99 is unacceptable. Suggest start with #1 reduce queue_limit and #2 enable early-reject for that tenant, and inform customer.
Jonathan - SRE: Agreed. I'll roll queue_limit -> 64 across shared-lowlatency-1 and enable early_reject threshold 80 for tenant paul-corp. Rolling now.
DeployBot: Rolling runtime-config change: set queue_limit=64 for pool shared-lowlatency-1 (canary 10% -> full)
SysOpsBot: Policy update applied: early_reject_threshold=80 for tenant paul-corp (effective immediately).
Anya - EngRuntime: Also recommend adjusting continuous_batching.max_wait_ms to 10ms for that pool to favor low latency; current is 25ms. That will reduce batch filling time for bursts of short requests.
Lee - Infra: Agreed. I'll queue that config change but want to monitor CPU/GPU utilization — smaller batches increase per-token overhead.
Jonathan - SRE: After queue_limit change, I see queue_depth dropping to ~30 in the next 90s, p95 down to ~350ms, p99 troughs to ~900ms. KV cache hit rate recovered a bit. No 5xx after early_reject policy applied.
Paul (Customer): I'm seeing behavior improve in my dashboard — p95 back to ~300-400ms, p99 ~1s. Thanks. We're happy to accept early_reject vs long tail.
Maria: Customer confirmed — marking as engaged; will follow up with root cause.
Anya - EngRuntime: Root cause summary draft: temporary config override increased queue_limit on shared-lowlatency-1 during a canary, which allowed queue to grow during a traffic burst consisting of many short single-token requests. Continuous batching attempted to fill large batches, increasing tail-latency and creating timeouts. Lowering queue_limit and enabling tenant early-reject reduced backlog and restored latency.
Anya - EngRuntime: Long-term actions: 1) revert temporary overrides by default and require approval; 2) add anomaly alert when queue_limit > baseline; 3) implement adaptive batching window that shrinks with high short-request ratio; 4) add tenant-specific backpressure routing to avoid hitting shared pools.
Lee - Infra: I'll open infra ticket to track reverting overrides and automating guardrail (INFRA-3492).
Jonathan - SRE: I'll add a runbook entry for this tail-latency pattern: checks for queue_limit drift, continuous-batching backlog, KV cache hit rate, and mitigation steps (reduce queue_limit, early_reject, route to dedicated).
Maria: I'll update the support ticket and propose a postmortem call with the customer tomorrow.
Paul (Customer): Appreciate the fast response. One more ask — can you share the exact commands you ran so we can reproduce mitigation in our staging?
Jonathan - SRE: Repro/mitigation snippet:
```
# lower queue limit on pool (admin only)
redwoodctl pools update shared-lowlatency-1 --set queue_limit=64
# set tenant early reject threshold
redwoodctl tenants update paul-corp --set early_reject=80
# adjust batching window for pool (opt-in)
redwoodctl pools update shared-lowlatency-1 --set continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=10
```
Maria: noted. I'll paste those in the support ticket.
DeployBot: Change complete: queue_limit rollback completed at 2311112298. No errors.
Jonathan - SRE: Follow-up: schedule for longer-term solution — adaptive batching tracker and guardrail automation. I'll assign tasks and link infra ticket.
Anya - EngRuntime: Also adding an eval to catch regressions where config overrides increase queue_limit beyond 1.5x baseline.
Paul (Customer): Thanks everyone. Will monitor and re-open if anything else shows up.
Maria: Closing incident thread for now — will reopen if customer reports recurrence. (reacted :white_check_mark:)
